Maria (CS Ops): Heads up — the new onboarding playbook automation we rolled out yesterday is firing for some accounts that have >1 active trial contact. Seeing duplicate touchpoints and a few customers flagged as 'at-risk' incorrectly.
Sam (CS Tools): Noted. Which rule specifically? Is it the 'no-owner dedupe' step or the webhook dedupe?
Maria (CS Ops): Looks like both. The dedupe check in the webhook handler is keyed by email but we have contacts with multiple emails and the playbook re-triggers when owner is blank. Example: acct 8352 had two contacts, different emails, both no owner — playbook fires twice.
Lee (AE): I saw that on my book — got two identical onboarding emails to the same company. Customers were confused.
Jordan (Data Eng): Can you paste the event payload for acct 8352? Might be helpful to see contact ids.
Maria (CS Ops): Sure — payload snippet: ```json
{"account_id":8352, "contacts":[{"id":9123, "email":"ops@acme.co"},{"id":9124, "email":"onboarding+ops@acme.co"}], "owner":null}```
Sam (CS Tools): OK — playbook-bot currently dedupes by email, then by contact id, then falls back to owner null check. That fallback is too permissive.
Sam (CS Tools): Proposed quick fix: change fallback to require both owner=null AND last_touch > 30d to avoid duplicating active handoffs. Also add a canary flag so only 10% of accounts hit new logic.
Maria (CS Ops): Agree on canary. We also need a manual override: CS owners should be able to mark a playbook instance as 'suppress' for 7 days.
Lee (AE): Good — I can take toggles for my accounts. How will suppression surface in the UI?
Sam (CS Tools): We'll expose a lightweight endpoint: POST /playbook/suppress {account_id, duration_days, reason}. UI checkbox will call it. playbook-bot will skip suppressed accounts.
Jordan (Data Eng): We should also adjust health scoring triggers — the automation bumped some accounts into 'renewal-risk' because the metric used 3-day event windows. I suggest moving to a 14-day window for engagement_decay in the scoring model.
Maria (CS Ops): 14-day window makes sense — the playbook was too reactive. Can we run a backtest for the last 90 days to see how many accounts would flip?
Jordan (Data Eng): Yep, I'll run a quick query: ```sql
SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS events_14d FROM events WHERE ts > now() - interval '14 days' GROUP BY account_id;```
Jordan (Data Eng): I'll do the backtest and post numbers in this thread by EOD.
Sam (CS Tools): Rollout plan I'm thinking: 1) Patch dedupe fallback and add suppression endpoint (hotfix, low-risk) -> deploy to staging. 2) Enable canary at 10% for 24h. 3) If metrics look good, increase to 50% -> 24h -> global. 4) Simultaneously run health-score backtest and adjust threshold if needed.
Maria (CS Ops): Sounds good. Who owns the hotfix? Sam?
Sam (CS Tools): I'll own the code change and staging deploy. Jordan will own the backtest and threshold recommendation. Maria will monitor CS tickets and be primary on-call for any customer escalations.
Lee (AE): Please add me to the canary list for my accounts: acct 9204, 8352, 8811.
Sam (CS Tools): Added — canary list updated. playbook-bot will tag messages for those accounts with :canary:.
playbook-bot: Deployed canary toggle update to staging. Use `/playbook status canary` to view active accounts.
Maria (CS Ops): One more ask — add a simple audit log for suppressed playbook triggers (who suppressed, when, reason). We need this for renewals sync.
Sam (CS Tools): Will add an audit table: playbook_suppression_log (account_id, user, expires_at, reason, created_at). Quick schema will be in PR.
Jordan (Data Eng): Backtest results: with 14d window, 7.2% fewer 'renewal-risk' flips across trial cohort — posting full numbers in a follow-up thread.
Maria (CS Ops): Thanks — let's proceed with the hotfix and 10% canary after Jordan's backtest artifacts land. I'll open a support tag and notify AEs.
Lee (AE): Thanks team.
Sam (CS Tools): I'll open PR #248 and link it here when ready. Expect staging deploy in ~2 hours.
playbook-bot: PR #248 created by Sam. CI checks passing.
